subject.title: [BUG] OpenAI Codex errors leak into user chat

question: When an unconfigured OpenAI/Codex path emits an error during subagent or coding-session startup, should OpenClaw drop that error before channel delivery or surface the existing generic safe failure copy?
rationale: The parser repair is mechanical, but changing unconfigured-provider failures from generic safe copy to silent discard affects provider routing, debugging, and channel semantics.

options.title: Land parser repair first
options.body: Recognize top-level string `detail` payloads and preserve the current generic user-facing error boundary while requiring live proof before adding silent discard.

options.title: Gate and drop unconfigured-provider failures
options.body: Add provider/auth gating so unconfigured OpenAI/Codex failures never reach channel delivery, with tests for configured and unconfigured provider paths.

options.title: Accept current generic suppression
options.body: Treat the raw leak as already mitigated by the channel-facing wrapper and close the remaining silent-discard request as not planned.

recommendation.title: Land parser repair first
recommendation.body: Recognize top-level string `detail` payloads and preserve the current generic user-facing error boundary while requiring live proof before adding silent discard.

likelyOwner.reason: This decision crosses formatter behavior, provider routing, and channel-visible delivery policy, and this account is the most recent area contributor in the available history.
